statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress eases to 51 in the elevated band: Iran's president stated on Saturday that the Strait of Hormuz would reopen if the United States ends its naval blockade, and said an Iran-Oman agreement on a shared route is due to be signed in Muscat on Monday before Arab foreign ministers, which firms the de-escalation channel against a still-shut East-West pipeline. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and the advance was broad. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly seven hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot in the forecast contains a tradeable session and no danger window is published. Third, the geopolitical channel firmed toward de-escalation this hour rather than toward escalation. Stress stays elevated at 51 because triple-digit crude, a shut 4-5 million barrel per day pipeline, an August core CPI print of +0.3% monthly and a Wednesday FOMC decision all remain unresolved.
headline: Nineteen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, and this hour the Hormuz de-escalation channel firmed: Iranian President Pezeshkian said the strait would reopen if the United States ends its naval blockade, and that Iran and Oman will sign an agreement on a shared route in Muscat on Monday before Arab foreign ministers, to be notified to the International Maritime Organisation, while the Saudi East-West pipeline remains shut with no repair timeline.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95%.

The material change this hour is geopolitical and points toward de-escalation. Yesterday's evidence was an Iranian foreign ministry confirmation that ministers would meet in Oman on Monday to discuss the strait. Today Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian went further in a Saturday interview, saying the Strait of Hormuz will reopen if the United States ends its naval blockade, and that Iran and Oman will sign an agreement on a shared route in Muscat on Monday in the presence of Arab foreign ministers, with the arrangement then notified to the International Maritime Organisation. That is a more concrete channel than a meeting to discuss, and it is the main reason Stress eases another point rather than holding.

Two items were checked and deliberately not treated as new escalation. Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao's remark that Iranian strikes 'blew the hell out of' Naval Support Activity Bahrain, reported on 11 September, is an official acknowledgment of damage sustained between February and June rather than a fresh event. A widely surfaced report describing steep Iranian conditions for reopening the strait was verified as dated 9 August and was therefore excluded from this hour's reasoning.

On the macro side, August CPI printed at 3.4% year over year with core at +0.3% monthly against +0.2% expected, and Friday reporting put market-implied odds of a September rate increase near 87%, up from about 72% a day earlier. The direction of Wednesday's decision is not asserted here; the event is carried in the calendar as a scheduled high-impact checkpoint that falls well outside this twenty-four-hour horizon. Crude is marked $100.05 after a 2.37% Friday decline that still left it up roughly 9.7% on the week, with the IEA demand downgrade and a raised EIA U.S. production path standing against the supply-side premium.

Because CME equity index futures do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, no slot in this horizon contains a tradeable session, so no danger window is published and conditional Tail stays inside the low band throughout, rising only from 6 to a ceiling of 12 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates toward that single repricing event.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 16:00 UTC on 11 September to 15:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens inside the U.S. afternoon that followed Friday's inflation print, with Tail between 13 and 17 in mixed mode and Stress at 80 decaying steadily as the event passed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since settled into a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final eighteen slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell monotonically from 80 to 52 across the twenty-four hours, and Confidence held inside the high band throughout, between 85 and 89. No slot in the window reached the 25-point Tail block threshold.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly seven hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps through 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 to a ceiling of 12 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs from 51 down to a floor of 47 through the overnight quiet, then edges back to 51 as the Monday Muscat signing and the reopen both approach with their outcomes unknown. Confidence decays from 85 to 80 purely as a function of a Friday-close evidence set ageing across a closed weekend.
